title: Physiological Sigh
opening: One optional sequence: two comfortable nasal inhales, the second added to the first, then a long mouth exhale. Keep it comfortable; skip it if unsuitable. Stop if uncomfortable or dizzy and return to ordinary breathing. You can explore the steps without trying them.

labels.sequenceIntro: Select a step to see where air moves.
labels.sequenceGroup: Choose a step in the optional sequence
labels.state: What does the person report feeling?
labels.scenarioIntro: Choose a sample combination; these are fictional, not recorded learner results.
labels.practice: Write a short plan for a real situation

sequence.title: First inhale · through nose
sequence.instruction: Breathe in comfortably through the nose.

sequence.title: Second inhale · add to first
sequence.instruction: Take a second comfortable nasal inhale, adding it to the first.

sequence.title: Exhale · through mouth
sequence.instruction: Exhale for a long, comfortable breath through the mouth.

preparations.title: Start the task directly
preparations.detail: No breathing preparation is used. Starting directly may be adequate.

preparations.title: Use comfortable ordinary breathing
preparations.detail: Continue ordinary comfortable breathing before the task. This is a comparison option, not a required technique.

preparations.title: Consider the optional sequence
preparations.detail: The person may choose the comfortable sequence, skip it, or stop immediately. No breathing exercise is needed for this lesson.

tasks.title: Explain one idea clearly
tasks.measure: Check whether the explanation includes the key idea and is understandable to its listener.

tasks.title: Recall three details
tasks.measure: Check which details are recalled accurately. A calmer feeling does not supply the recall result.

tasks.title: Solve a reasoning problem
tasks.measure: Check whether the reasoning reaches a supported answer. A calmer feeling does not establish correctness.

interpretations.calmer-clear: The person reports feeling calmer, and the selected task check is met in this scenario. Keep the two observations separate; this single example does not show the preparation caused the task result.
interpretations.calmer-missed: The person reports feeling calmer, while the selected task check is not met. A calmer feeling does not prove improved memory, reasoning, or communication.
interpretations.calmer-unknown: The person reports feeling calmer, but the task result was not checked. The task outcome remains unknown.
interpretations.same-clear: The person reports no felt change, while the selected task check is met. A felt change is not required to establish this one task result.
interpretations.same-missed: Neither a felt change nor a successful task check is reported in this scenario. There is no basis here for claiming benefit.
interpretations.same-unknown: No felt change is reported and the task result was not checked. The task outcome remains unknown.
interpretations.uncomfortable-clear: The task check is met, but the person feels uncomfortable. Stop or skip the breathing option; a task result does not make discomfort a reason to continue.
interpretations.uncomfortable-missed: The person feels uncomfortable and the selected task check is not met. Stop the option and return to ordinary breathing; do not repeat it to dizziness or strain.
interpretations.uncomfortable-unknown: The person feels uncomfortable and the task result was not checked. Stop the option; the task outcome remains unknown.

practice.prediction: In the situation you have in mind, what change in felt state would you expect, if any? Mark uncertainty plainly; this is not a prediction of better performance.
practice.observation: Without doing a breathing exercise, describe the source sequence in order and say whether it is optional.
practice.comparison: Compare starting directly, comfortable ordinary breathing, and considering the optional sequence. What would each comparison help you learn?
practice.result: Name the task you would check. What separate observation would tell you whether that task result was met?
practice.revision: What would make you skip or stop the option, or decide it did not help this task?
practice.step: Transfer the same distinction to another task: how would you record felt state and task result as separate observations?

source.externalContext: R05 NCCIH — Meditation and Mindfulness: Effectiveness and Safety
